title: Applying for a US Visa from Germany: Do You Need a Flight Booking?
metaTitle: US Visa from Germany: Do You Need a Flight Booking?
metaDescription: US Mission guidance says you do not need tickets to apply, and not to book travel until the visa is issued. What German applicants should show instead.
excerpt: You do not need to buy a flight ticket to apply for a US visa from Germany, and US Mission posts recommend you wait until the visa is issued. German passport holders travel on ESTA and skip the B1/B2 process altogether. Non-EU residents on an Aufenthaltstitel can show a flight reservation instead of a purchase.
quickAnswer: No, you do not need a flight ticket to apply for a US visa from Germany. US Mission guidance says you do not need confirmed travel dates or airplane tickets to apply, and recommends you do not book travel until the visa is issued. An unticketed reservation with a real GDS PNR documents your plan for from EUR 12.
content:
No, you do not need to buy a flight ticket to apply for a US visa from Germany, and the consulates would rather you did not. US Mission guidance states plainly that you do not need confirmed travel dates or airplane tickets to apply, and recommends you hold off on booking until the visa has been issued. If a form or an officer asks what your trip looks like, a flight reservation answers that without you spending hundreds of euros.

Do German citizens need a US visa at all?

German passport holders almost never need a B1/B2 visa for a short trip. Germany is a member of the Visa Waiver Programme, so German citizens travelling for business, pleasure or transit apply for an ESTA instead and stay up to 90 days.

The conditions are specific. You need your own full-validity e-passport, a stay of no more than 90 days, and you must be flying with a carrier that participates in the programme. Temporary passports, the Vorläufige Reisepass, are not eligible.

There is one condition in that list that catches people out. US Mission Germany states that VWP travellers must hold a valid return or onward ticket, and that onward tickets may not end in Canada, Mexico or the Caribbean.

Read that condition literally. The programme asks for a ticket, and an unticketed reservation is not a ticket, so a flight reservation does not satisfy the Visa Waiver Programme requirement on its own.

Where a verifiable reservation does belong is a visa application, or an airline or border officer elsewhere who accepts a booking as evidence of onward travel. For visa-free travel to the United States, buy the ticket.

Who applying from Germany actually needs a B1/B2 visa?

The B1/B2 audience in Germany is mostly non-EU nationals who live here. If you hold an Aufenthaltstitel as an Indian, Pakistani, Nigerian, Turkish, Filipino or other non-VWP national, your German residence permit lets you live and work in Germany but it does not put you in the Visa Waiver Programme. Your nationality decides that.

You can still apply from Germany rather than flying home to do it. US Mission Germany's notice says nonimmigrant visa applicants should schedule their interview at the US Embassy or Consulate in their country of residence or nationality, and Germany is your country of residence.

For this group the flight booking question is live. You are facing an interview date, a nonrefundable fee, and a visa that might take longer than you planned, so what you do about flights matters.

Does the US government tell you not to buy a ticket before your visa is issued?

Yes, and US Mission posts say it in blunt terms. The US Embassy in Vienna tells applicants: "You do NOT need confirmed travel dates or airplane tickets to apply for a visa. In fact, we recommend you do not book any travel until your visa has been issued."

The US Embassy in Bern puts the same point even more directly, advising applicants they are strongly advised not to book their travel before they have received their visa. The reasoning is the same at every post, including the German ones. A visa is not guaranteed on the day of the interview, and passports go back out by post afterwards.

There is a second reason to be careful with money at this stage. US Mission Germany states that visa application fees are non-refundable and non-transferable, so the fee is already a sunk cost before you add a flight to it.

We have written about the wider version of this question in should you buy a flight ticket before visa approval. The short version holds for Germany too. Buying early buys you nothing with the consular officer and transfers all the risk to you.

So what do you show if you have not bought a ticket?

You show a reservation rather than a purchase. The DS-160 asks about your planned trip, and the officer wants a trip that makes sense against your job, your residence permit and your ties to Germany. A flight reservation documents the plan at a cost you can throw away.

That is the whole point of a dummy ticket for a visa application. It is a real booking in the airline's reservation system that was never paid for, so it shows dates, routing, your name and a booking reference, and then it quietly expires.

Keep the reservation honest and keep it boring. Use your name exactly as it appears in your passport, pick dates that match what you typed into the DS-160, and route the trip the way a real traveller would.

Where do you attend a US visa interview in Germany?

Three posts in Germany handle visas. US Mission Germany confirms that visa services are offered at the US Consulates General in Frankfurt and Munich and at the US Embassy in Berlin, and that the consulates in Hamburg, Leipzig and Düsseldorf do not offer visa services.

Appointments and fees do not go through the embassy directly. The mission names US Travel Docs as its official visa service provider in Germany and the only private company authorised to handle visa information and application processing there.

Not every applicant sits an interview. US Mission Germany says that for some visa categories, travellers who are German citizens or permanent residents may apply by mail without an in-person appearance, and it encourages eligible applicants to use that route. Check your own category before you assume you need a slot in Frankfurt.

What is a dummy ticket from Dummy Ticket 365?

It is an unticketed flight reservation that carries a real six-character PNR. We create it on Amadeus, Sabre or Travelport, the same global distribution systems that travel agents and airlines use, and it arrives in your inbox within minutes.

It is not a paid ticket and we never pretend otherwise. There is no e-ticket number behind it and no money has changed hands with the airline, which is exactly why it costs a few euros instead of a few hundred.

It is also not a hotel booking or any other document. We sell one thing, which is the flight reservation, and that keeps the product simple to check.

Can a consulate verify the reservation?

Verification happens in the GDS, not on an airline's public website. A consular officer or an airline agent with GDS access can pull the record by its six-character reference and see the segments, the dates and the passenger name.

This matters because of a quirk that worries a lot of applicants. Most airlines display only ticketed bookings in the "manage my booking" section of their own site, so a live unticketed reservation often will not show up there even while it is perfectly valid in the GDS. Emirates and Etihad are the usual exceptions.

If that distinction is new to you, read how embassies verify flight reservations through the GDS before your interview. Knowing where your booking is visible, and where it is not, stops you panicking the night before.

How much does a dummy ticket cost in Germany?

Pricing is by validity, in euros on our Germany page. A reservation valid for 2 days is EUR 12, 7 days is EUR 17, and 14 days is EUR 19. In dollars those are USD 13, USD 19 and USD 21.

Pick the validity around your appointment, not around your trip. A 2-day reservation is fine if your interview is the day after tomorrow, and the 14-day option gives you room if you are assembling documents over a fortnight.

Compare that against a refundable transatlantic fare out of Frankfurt and the maths answers itself. You are documenting a plan, not buying a seat you cannot yet use.

What if the reservation expires before the visa comes through?

An expired reservation is not a problem, because it was never meant to outlive the appointment. The consulate looks at your documents on the day of your interview, so the reservation needs to be live then, not three weeks later while your passport is in the post.

If your case goes into further administrative processing, you simply do not have a reliable date to book around. That is the exact situation the US posts are warning about when they tell you to wait.

We cover the timing in what to do when your flight reservation expires before visa approval. The practical answer is to issue the reservation close to the date it will be seen and buy the real ticket once the visa is in your passport.

Will a dummy ticket get your visa refused?

A valid reservation is not a refusal reason by itself. B1/B2 decisions turn on whether you have shown strong ties to your home or residence country and a credible temporary purpose, and a flight reservation is one small supporting document in that picture.

What does cause trouble is a fake document. A PDF edited in a graphics tool, a booking reference that returns nothing in the GDS, or dates that contradict your DS-160 all undermine you, which is the opposite of what the document is for.

So the rule is simple. If you use a reservation, use a real one that a trained agent can look up, and keep every detail consistent with the rest of your file.

What else should a Germany-based applicant have ready?

Your residence in Germany is the strongest part of your file, so document it. The residence permit itself, your employment contract or payslips, and anything that shows you are coming back, such as study enrolment or a tenancy, all speak to the temporary purpose a B1/B2 visa requires.

Keep your DS-160 and your paperwork telling one story. If the form says a two-week trip in March and your reservation shows three weeks in April, you have created a question you did not need to answer at the counter.

Officers decide on the whole picture, not on one document. A flight reservation supports the plan, and nobody has ever been issued a visa because of the booking alone.

Can the same reservation help at check-in or at the border?

Yes, and this is where the document earns its keep after the visa stage. Airlines check that one-way passengers can leave again before they let them board, and border officers ask the same thing in their own way.

Visa Waiver Programme travellers face a version of this too. US Mission Germany lists a valid return or onward ticket among the conditions for visa-free travel, and says onward tickets may not end in Canada, Mexico or the Caribbean.

A GDS reservation under your passport name covers that check in the moment it is made. Size the validity to the day you fly rather than the week you booked it.

What should you do before your appointment in Germany?

Work in this order and you will not waste money. Confirm whether you need a visa at all, because if you hold a German passport you are an ESTA traveller rather than a B1/B2 applicant.

If you do need the visa, complete the DS-160, book through US Travel Docs for Frankfurt, Munich or Berlin, and assemble your supporting documents without buying flights. Add a reservation sized to your appointment date, sit the interview, and buy the real ticket when the passport comes back with the visa in it.

When you are ready, order from our German pricing page and it lands in your email in minutes with a PNR you can check. That is one less thing to think about on interview day.

faqs.question: Do I need a flight ticket to apply for a US visa from Germany?
faqs.answer: No. US Mission guidance states you do not need confirmed travel dates or airplane tickets to apply, and recommends not booking travel until the visa has been issued. A flight reservation documents your intended trip for the DS-160 and the interview without you committing money to a date you do not control yet.

faqs.question: Do German citizens need a B1/B2 visa for the United States?
faqs.answer: Usually not. Germany is in the Visa Waiver Programme, so German passport holders apply for an approved ESTA before boarding and may stay up to 90 days for business, pleasure or transit. You need a full-validity e-passport, and temporary German passports are not eligible for visa-free travel.

faqs.question: I live in Germany on an Aufenthaltstitel. Can I apply here?
faqs.answer: Yes. US Mission Germany says nonimmigrant applicants should schedule their interview at the US Embassy or Consulate in their country of residence or nationality, and Germany counts as your country of residence. Your residence permit does not place you in the Visa Waiver Programme, so your nationality still decides whether you need a B1/B2 visa.

faqs.question: Which US consulates in Germany hold visa interviews?
faqs.answer: Visa services run at the US Consulates General in Frankfurt and Munich and at the US Embassy in Berlin. The consulates in Hamburg, Leipzig and Düsseldorf do not offer visa services. Appointments and fees go through US Travel Docs, the mission's official visa service provider in Germany.

faqs.question: Can the consulate check my dummy ticket?
faqs.answer: Yes, through the GDS. Our reservations carry a real six-character PNR created on Amadeus, Sabre or Travelport, so an officer or airline agent with GDS access can pull the record. Most airline websites show only ticketed bookings, so an unticketed reservation often will not appear there, with Emirates and Etihad the usual exceptions.

faqs.question: What does a dummy ticket cost if I am applying from Germany?
faqs.answer: Pricing follows validity: EUR 12 for 2 days, EUR 17 for 7 days and EUR 19 for 14 days, which is USD 13, USD 19 and USD 21. Choose the validity that covers your interview date, since the reservation only needs to be live when your documents are seen.
